title: Republican Bill Cassidy blames administration vaccine policy for measles deaths
description_short: Republican Bill Cassidy blames administration vaccine policy for measles deaths
description_medium: At a September 16, 2026 Senate health-nominee hearing, Republican Senator Bill Cassidy blamed administration vaccine messaging and policy for recent measles deaths. He pressed surgeon-general nominee Nicole Saphier to reject a vaccine-autism link; she said in her testimony that she did not believe childhood vaccines cause autism.
description_long: At a September 16, 2026 Senate hearing on the surgeon-general nomination, Republican Senator Bill Cassidy criticized the administration’s vaccine messaging and policy in connection with recent measles deaths. Cassidy pressed nominee Nicole Saphier to reject the claim that childhood vaccines cause autism. Saphier eventually said she did not believe childhood vaccines cause autism. The exchange brought two questions into the confirmation process: how the administration’s public statements about vaccination relate to measles outbreaks, and whether the nominee would affirm the medical consensus on vaccine safety. Cassidy’s statement about the deaths was an accusation made during questioning, not a finding that a particular policy caused an individual death. Cassidy’s accusation connected the administration’s public-health messaging to the outbreak’s most serious consequences, but his statement alone did not establish that any particular policy caused a death. The exchange put pressure on the nominee to address both the administration’s public position and the evidence on vaccine safety.
